title: Provider run identity and usage telemetry
description: Objective: provide the missing production provider-run telemetry source required by the benchmark harness. Deliverable: runner/provider records and a public consumer surface that bind each run to provider/model ID, model snapshot or build evidence, reasoning effort, runtime/profile identities, start/completion/stop classification, token and step measurements, infrastructure classification, achieved concurrency, and provider-neutral usage/cost evidence through the landed scheduler measurement contract. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 2b15b8f: Claude runtime/launch observations bind runtime bytes, streams, exit and timestamps but contain no selected model ID/snapshot/reasoning effort, usage cost, stop reason, infrastructure class, step count, or concurrency; scheduler budget-contract/measurement has the six source/coverage semantics but is not root-exported and has no production provider emitter/consumer. Consumer: task-b937811e8b72459ea169e5fff1238ce1. NOT in scope: benchmark gate statistics, competitor records, pricing comparison, corpus/campaign execution, or claims. Owned paths: focused runner provider telemetry modules, minimal scheduler curated export if necessary, public runner surface, and focused tests. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.
definitionOfDone: A frozen production provider-run record binds run/effect identity, provider, selected model ID, snapshot/build evidence, reasoning effort, runtime observation/profile digests, start/completion timestamps, exact terminal classification, token count, step count, and achieved/concurrency-ceiling values; missing provider facts are explicit UNKNOWN with stable reason code/layer, never zero.

Provider usage observations are normalized through the existing scheduler UsageMeasurementRecord/normalizeUsageMeasurement semantics, preserve COMPLETE/PARTIAL/UNKNOWN and exact source provenance, and publish cost-basis metadata without converting PARTIAL or UNKNOWN into complete spend.

The real Claude launch/result path emits or durably hands off the record through a curated @moe/runner root surface; tests use that production call path rather than constructing a benchmark-only mirror.

Closed terminal/infra/concurrency vocabularies distinguish administrative wall cap, token/step exhaustion, product cap, agent failure, provider/rate/container infrastructure failure and ordinary completion where observed; unknown/unreadable termination retains its exact code/layer.

Focused tests assert every declared outcome and measurement source is generated with non-zero exact cardinality, pin exact UNKNOWN code/layer, and mutation-check the production model/effort and usage-coverage comparisons.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test exits 0.
taskRails: Runtime version/closure is not model snapshot/build evidence; record both and never substitute profileRevisionId for model/effort.
UNKNOWN/PARTIAL token or cost evidence is never zero or complete. Preserve scheduler source/coverage authority rather than copying it into the benchmark package.
No confirmatory corpus/campaign or claim verdict code belongs in this task.
Tests assert exact stable reason code and refusing layer and generated case counts are non-zero.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; the cap is per file.
reopenReason: Human-directed next unblock after live architect audit: existing runner launch/runtime observations and scheduler usage-measurement semantics are landed; the measured missing capability is the production provider/model/effort/usage telemetry and public consumer edge owned by this task. Keep UNKNOWN/PARTIAL evidence fail-closed.

comments.author: worker-733c82bb
comments.content:
CONSUMER EDGE from task-5fa25bb33e974f04865b46f9fa0f3910 — the provider-neutral usage measurement authority is now reachable from the BARE package root `@moe/scheduler`. Import it; do not copy the source/coverage matrix and do not deep-import into ./budget/ (the package `exports` map is exclusive — `{".": "./src/index.ts"}` — so a subpath will not resolve for you).

PUBLISHED VALUES (7), all runtime bindings, verified loading and invoking under plain Node via the bare specifier:
  normalizeUsageMeasurement          (function)
  MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_CODES            (frozen array, 10 codes)
  MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_LAYERS           (frozen array, exactly ["CONTRACT","MEASUREMENT"])
  SUPPORTED_SOURCE_PARSER_VERSIONS   (frozen array, exactly [1, 2])
  BUDGET_ISSUE_CODES                 (frozen array — the CONTRACT-layer vocabulary)
  BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_COVERAGES       (frozen array, ["COMPLETE","PARTIAL","UNKNOWN"])
  BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_SOURCES         (frozen array, 6 sources)

PUBLISHED TYPES (11), the full callable closure:
  UsageMeasurementRecord, ObservedIntervalRefs, BudgetMeasurementCoverage, BudgetMeasurementSource,
  BudgetIssueCode, NormalizedMeasurement, PricebookBinding, MeasurementResult, LayeredIssue,
  MeasurementIssueCode, MeasurementIssueLayer.
ObservedIntervalRefs is included deliberately: it is the field type of UsageMeasurementRecord.observedInterval, so without it you could name the record but never construct one.

SIGNATURE
  normalizeUsageMeasurement(input: unknown, prior?: NormalizedMeasurement | null): MeasurementResult<NormalizedMeasurement>

`input` is the ENVELOPE, not the measurement — exactly `{ measurement, pricebookBinding, truncated }` with no extra keys. Anything else refuses MEASUREMENT : BUDGET_OBSERVATION_MALFORMED. Result is a discriminated union: `{ ok: true, record }` or `{ ok: false, issues: readonly LayeredIssue[] }`, and every issue carries both a `layer` and a `code` — narrow on `layer` before reading `code`, because the CONTRACT arm is typed BudgetIssueCode and the MEASUREMENT arm MeasurementIssueCode.

`prior` is the last ACCEPTED observation of the same stream, supplied by you — the normalizer keeps no state. Behaviour with a prior: a same-identity same-bytes redelivery is a DETERMINISTIC NO-OP that returns the exact prior object (reference-identical, `toBe`, not a fresh equal one), so retry/at-least-once delivery is safe. Only the immediate successor sequence is accepted; a skip refuses BUDGET_OBSERVATION_SEQUENCE_GAP, a rewind BUDGET_OBSERVATION_SEQUENCE_REGRESSION, same identity with different bytes BUDGET_OBSERVATION_IDENTITY_CONFLICT, and a foreign providerRunRef BUDGET_OBSERVATION_STREAM_MISMATCH.

DELIBERATELY WITHHELD, so the composer cannot route around the authority:
  validateUsageMeasurement — the normalizer COMPOSES it and then adds the source/coverage matrix, the pricebook-binding check and the identity/sequence checks. Holding the bare validator would let you accept records the authority refuses.
  projectBudgetFact / PolicyFactInputCompatible / MEASUREMENT_FACT_TIER — budget-policy projection is a different seam. If you need a fact projection, ask for that seam to be published rather than reconstructing it.
Also absent by design: validateBudgetAccount, validateReserveDeclaration, MAX_BUDGET_METERS. Their absence is pinned by a negative-control test, so a future widening is a deliberate reviewed act.

ONE CAVEAT WORTH KNOWING. NormalizedMeasurement is a plain published interface, so TypeScript will let you hand-write one. Do not — `identity` is computed by the normalizer and the returned record is deeply frozen and detached from your input. Only a record that came out of normalizeUsageMeasurement carries authority; a hand-built one is an unvalidated claim wearing the right type.

Evidence: packages/scheduler/src/index-surface.test.ts pins the exact namespace (85 root exports, hand-written count) and drives UNKNOWN/null, PARTIAL lower-bound, the full 6x3 source-by-coverage sweep, truncated-completion, pricebook binding, uncorrelated billing claim, both malformed layers and the sequence guards entirely through the bare root. A mutation drill on the production kernel's emitted code reddened those root tests, which is the proof the root binding is the production normalizer and not a re-export of something weaker.

PRODUCER RECORD from task-d23a913f0586431d9dccc0cfd1f66fd5 (Bind Claude model and effort launch selection). Two records: (A) what landed and how to consume it, (B) an unresolved NAME DISAGREEMENT this task did NOT reconcile unilaterally — that call belongs to this task's architect.

=== (A) WHAT LANDED, EXACT SPELLINGS ===

New module: packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-launch-selection.ts (+ its enforced .js bridge).

PUBLISHED ON THE @moe/runner ROOT (values):
  CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_FLAGS   // { model: "--model", effort: "--reasoning-effort" }
  CLAUDE_MODEL_EVIDENCE_KINDS     // ["DATED_SNAPSHOT", "BUILD_STAMP", "UNKNOWN"]
  CLAUDE_REASONING_EFFORTS        // ["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", "UNKNOWN"]
PUBLISHED (types): ClaudeLaunchSelection, ClaudeModelEvidenceKind, ClaudeReasoningEffort.

ClaudeLaunchRequest gained ONE field, `launchSelection: ClaudeLaunchSelection`, whose ten fields are spelled EXACTLY:
  provider ("claude") | selectedModelId | modelSnapshotKind | modelSnapshotEvidence |
  reasoningEffort | profileRevisionId | configurationDigest | policyDigest |
  orchestrationDigest | concurrencyCeiling
Constraints worth knowing before you construct one: selectedModelId and profileRevisionId must be non-whitespace printable tokens (the daemon wrapper spawns with shell:true on win32, where a space in a model id is shredded); the three digests must match /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/; concurrencyCeiling must be a positive safe integer; and modelSnapshotKind === "UNKNOWN" if and only if modelSnapshotEvidence === "UNKNOWN" — absent evidence stays absent and present evidence may not borrow the absence literal, in either direction.

DELIBERATELY WITHHELD: snapshotLaunchSelection and verifyLaunchSelection are NOT on the root, and there is a negative control test asserting their absence. launchClaude applies both itself. Publishing them would let a consumer pre-validate one selection and then hand launchClaude a different one — the exact disagreement the seam exists to prevent. Do not plan against them.

REFUSAL VOCABULARY: layer TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION (appended to CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LAYERS), seven codes appended to CLAUDE_LAUNCH_ERROR_CODES: CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_MALFORMED, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_MODEL_{UNPROVEN,AMBIGUOUS,MISMATCH}, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_EFFORT_{UNPROVEN,AMBIGUOUS,MISMATCH}. Model and effort carry SEPARATE codes on purpose so either comparison can be broken alone; mutation drills D1/D2 confirmed each family reddens without the other.

GATE POSITION: after the duplicate short-circuit, before prepareRuntime — so ahead of runtime preparation, grant consumption, lock acquisition and boundary open. An unproven selection produces an exactly-empty dependency log. Alias-only argv is refused as MISMATCH (an alias never string-equals a dated exact id); duplicate flags refuse as AMBIGUOUS whether or not the values agree.

=== DoD 5 CONSUMER CLAUSE, STATED PLAINLY ===
Satisfied as ROOT REACHABILITY plus this recorded task id — NOT as a compiling import. This task landed no call site in your package, because task-159 is BLOCKED behind four prerequisites, none DONE. Nothing here imports the selection; the launcher composes it internally. When task-159 unblocks, the composing edge is yours to land.

=== (B) NAME DISAGREEMENT — FOR THIS TASK'S ARCHITECT TO RESOLVE ===
Three mismatches between task-159's wording and the DoD task-d23a913f implemented verbatim:

1. DIGEST NOUNS ARE DISJOINT. task-159 asks for runtime observation/profile digests. task-d23a913f's DoD specifies configuration/policy/orchestration digests, and those are the three fields that shipped. Zero occurrences of the latter noun set in task-159. Somebody has to decide whether these are the same three digests under two names or genuinely different evidence; I did not assume.

2. CONCURRENCY IS HALF DELIVERED, BY DESIGN. task-159 wants achieved AND ceiling as a pair. This task's DoD names only the ceiling, and only concurrencyCeiling shipped. The achieved half belongs to task-cbc42f (BACKLOG, hard-depends on this task). Planning against an `achievedConcurrency` field today would plan against a symbol that does not exist.

3. profileRevisionId IS POSITIVE HERE, PROHIBITED THERE — both true at once, and a careless reading inverts one. task-159 names it only as a prohibition ("never substitute it for model/effort"). This task carries it as a POSITIVE field on the selection record. The prohibition is honoured and enforced: a test proves runtime reportedVersion, pinned closure and profileRevisionId can NEVER satisfy the model or effort requirement — set those and nothing else and you get CLAUDE_LAUNCH_MODEL_UNPROVEN. The field exists to be carried as separate evidence, never to stand in.
